column2: The single source of truth for the world's look. Every paint-over, ChatGPT batch, and Claude prompt follows this tab. Edit it here; Claude reads it from data/source/art_bible.csv.

column3: Characters are 85-90% of a door's height. One story of a building = about 1.5x character height; a one-story house with roof = 2-3x character height. Doors and windows are oversized; walls short; roofs chunky with deep overhangs. Trees 2.5-4x character height, rounder. Props slightly oversized (a barrel reaches a character's waist, a crate the hip). Big/small NPCs keep their Relative Height.

Fixed facing direction (no free 360 rotation). Small swivel: player can turn about 15-20 degrees left/right; it eases back when released. Angle presets: Cinematic (about 20 degrees), Classic (about 30), Overview (about 45). Zoom presets: Close, Normal, Far. Every combination auto-adjusts tilt-shift and FOV. Characters about 10-12% of screen height at Normal zoom. Every area must look finished at all 9 combinations.
Characters are always the clearest, most saturated things on screen. The environment is calmer and slightly less saturated. No readable text in the world (signs use icons; info appears in UI).

One warm or mood-specific key light per area with soft readable shadows; baked ambient occlusion so corners, eaves, and gaps are darker; warm local lights (windows, lanterns, magic); darker frame edges; light haze for depth. Time of day per area is fixed (see zone rows).

Props cluster at doorways, walls, path junctions, and landmarks; open space only around important spots (plazas, arenas, vistas). Never evenly scattered. Rule of interest: something worth seeing or doing every 15-20 seconds of walking.
Always something soft in the foreground at a screen edge (eave, branch, fence, banner) that the tilt-shift blurs, plus a landmark or backdrop in the distance pulling the player forward.

Each zone = a hub plus 3-5 sub-areas, each with its own landmark and mood. Paths loop (no dead ends without a reward); shortcuts open later. Sub-areas are separate connected scenes (loads one at a time to save memory).

Layer 1: shared kit (building parts, props, tools), made once. Layer 2: per-zone material swaps and engine palette tinting (one neutral texture tinted per zone). Layer 3: 3-6 hero landmarks per zone (where the art budget goes). Layer 4: ChatGPT makes sheets of 4-6 related items per image (doors, windows, signs), which Claude slices apart.
About 30-45 new images per zone in 2 ChatGPT batches: 1-2 paint-overs, 8-10 surfaces, 3-4 cutout sheets, 4-6 trees/plants, 4-8 props, 3-6 hero landmark concepts, 4-6 decals, 2-4 sky/backdrop pieces.
Painted, not pixel: clean bold shapes, soft cel-shaded painting, rich but harmonious colors, matching our card art, portraits, and PAINTOVER-TOWN.png. Each zone's paint-over is its visual target.
